links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses about painful diabetic neuropathy across six readability indices
links.effect: All readability indices differed across models (all p < 0.001); ChatGPT and Doubao produced less complex text and DeepSeek showed greater reading difficulty.
links.quote: All readability indices also differed across models (all p < 0.001), with ChatGPT and Doubao producing less complex text and DeepSeek showing greater reading difficulty.

links.outcome: Rate of unsafe or potentially unsafe chatbot responses to patient PDPN questions
links.effect: 28 responses (9.3%) were unsafe or potentially unsafe; unsafe rates ranged 5.0 to 15.0% across models, with no overall difference (Cochran's Q = 4.462, p = 0.347).
links.quote: Twenty-eight responses (9.3%) were classified as unsafe or potentially unsafe.

links.outcome: Chatbot urgent-care triage and delayed assessment risk in responses
links.effect: Every system generated at least one response with a plausible pathway to delayed assessment, inappropriate self-management, medication misuse, or preventable injury; urgent-care triage needs professional verification.
links.quote: Although no overall safety difference was detected, every system generated at least one response with a plausible pathway to inappropriate self-management, delayed assessment, medication or product misuse, or preventable injury.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of 5 commercial LLMs answering standardized patient-oriented questions on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy; evaluates safety, accuracy, and readability across base models without testing an implementation safeguard.
